rounds.title: ROUND 3 · LIFT 3 BALLS
rounds.question: 3 in. How many out?
fact: The middle ball swings both ways

rounds.title: FINAL · LET IT RUN
rounds.question: Does it clack forever?
fact: Lab test: in sync after 1–2 min

explain.title: WHY?
lines: Small losses sync all the balls

source: Hutzler et al., Am. J. Phys. 72, 1508 (2004)
caption: Lift 2 balls on a Newton's cradle: how many fly out? 1, 2 or 3? 🤔 And does it really clack forever? Drop your bet 👇 #newtonscradle #physics #science #satisfying #mythbusting #3danimation
description: We test a Newton's cradle: five steel balls hanging in a row. We lift 1 ball, then 2, then 3, release them and count how many balls fly out on the other side. Then we let it run to see if it clacks forever.

Lift 1 ball and exactly 1 flies out; lift 2 and 2 fly out; lift 3 and 3 fly out, so the middle ball swings out on both sides. It is never 1 ball flying out twice as fast: that would keep the momentum (2 x m x v = m x 2v) but double the energy, which is impossible. Only the same number of balls at the same speed keeps both momentum and energy.

It does not clack forever. In a 2004 lab study (Hutzler, Delaney, Weaire and MacLeod, American Journal of Physics), the balls lost a little energy at every clack and, after 1 to 2 minutes, all the balls were swinging together as one block, each with a much smaller swing.
The animation is a simulation: each ball is a real pendulum and the balls touch through a Hertz contact with a small energy loss, the same model as in that study.
sources_detail: Hutzler, Delaney, Weaire & MacLeod, 'Rocking Newton's cradle', Am. J. Phys. 72(12), 1508-1516 (2004): with a lab cradle (metal balls 6.8 cm, 0.7 kg, 1.3 m wires), 'the time required for the system of balls to settle into the collective mode is between 1 and 2 min'; the collective amplitude is theta0/N; dissipation in the collisions brings the balls into phase.

Momentum and energy: lift n balls of mass m to speed v. Momentum n m v and energy n m v^2 / 2 are both conserved only if n balls leave at v (k balls at speed u: k u = n v and k u^2 = n v^2 give u = v, k = n). Example n = 2: one ball at 2v keeps momentum (2mv) but has energy 2 m v^2, twice the 1 m v^2 that came in.

Simulated: 5 pendulums (ball 10 cm, wire 0.45 m, lift 26 degrees), Hertz contact F = k d^1.5 with Hunt-Crossley damping (lambda 0.15 s/m), 0.5 mm gap between balls. Time-lapse clock = simulation time; in the simulation the balls settle into one swing (about 1/5 of the lift angle) within the 1-2 min seen in the lab.
